decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already records the single-board architecture, board count, removal of the obsolete separate-board list, and integrated-board scope.

This Requirement is scoped to the legacy main and sensor boards and their interboard cabling; the source proposes a new integrated-board design and does not retroactively revise the legacy board layout.

The existing same-message MODIFY already integrates the external sensor fanout onto the single board, disables interboard connectors, removes obsolete interboard-input and total-count attributes, and updates scope.

The candidate describes the milestone-local legacy multi-board interface. The source establishes a separate integrated-board design but does not alter the historical connector and pinout requirements of the legacy boards.
The source's component-selection policy applies to the new integrated board and does not change the task-local readiness or optional connector population of the legacy main-board BOM.
The source does not change the existing power-board BOM obligations concerning assembly readiness, capacitor part numbers, or justification of unplanned components.
Changing the architecture of a new integrated design does not modify the task-local requirement to deliver the specified fabrication and placement exports for the legacy sensor board.
The source does not alter the task-local requirement for a correct board-specific BOM for the legacy sensor board.
The source does not specify the integrated board's dimensions, orientation, mounting holes, USB-C placement, or enclosure fit and does not revise the legacy power-board form factor.
Eliminating interboard connectors in the new integrated design does not retroactively change the milestone-local battery connector accessibility and placement constraints of the legacy power board.
The source does not state a layer count for the integrated board or revise the four-layer requirement of the legacy main board.
Reducing the number of connectors does not remove or change the requirement to mark the pins of connectors that remain.
